title: Prefix count is strictly smaller
statement: Let $l$ be a finite list, let $i$ be a natural number with $i<\operatorname{length}(l)$, and let $x$ and $d$ be elements of its type. If the element at position $i$, using $d$ as the default when that position is unavailable, is $x$, then the number of occurrences of $x$ among the first $i$ entries is strictly less than its number of occurrences in $l$.
hypotheses_covered: Elements $x$ and $d$ of the list's type
